descriptions: one, eternally free (anādimukta), omniscient and omnipotent
a mass of consciousness, pervasive, ever-risen, tranquil, who favours all (Tattvaprakāśa 1)
acts by a single conscious power (śakti) and has no body of māyā; for worship, a body of mantras
performs the five acts for the souls' release
negations: not the material cause of the world
relation_to_self: Souls are eternal and many, distinct from Śiva; freed, each becomes equal to Śiva (a 'Śiva') in knowledge and agency without becoming him.
relation_to_world: The world is real, produced from māyā (and bindu) as material cause, with Śiva as efficient cause; it exists to ripen and release souls.
caveat: Accepts one supreme Lord but denies that souls and māyā are his appearances; a 'one truth' reading that collapses souls or the world into Śiva is rejected.

names.name: the Lord of the Dance (Naṭarājaṉ, Ampalavāṇaṉ)

descriptions: the Real (cat), known neither as a sense-object nor as nothing, but by grace
pervades all as the vowel 'a' pervades letters (Tiruvaruṭpayaṉ 1.1)
grace (aruḷ) is his power, and he comes as the guru
dances the five acts at Chidambaram
negations: not the object of the senses (Civañāṉa Pōtam 6)
not one with souls in substance; not two in separation
relation_to_self: Advaita as inseparability: one with, other than, and together with souls; the freed soul abides in him enjoying his bliss.
relation_to_world: Efficient cause of the real world produced from māyā; the world is 'acat' only as perishing, not as illusion.
caveat: The Tamil school calls its view non-dual but insists on three eternal realities; it rejects Advaita's identity and unreality of the world.

names.name: the Lord of each shrine (Tillaiyampalavāṇaṉ, Ārūraṉ …)

descriptions: the one whom the Vedas call 'not this, not this', who came as guru and took the devotee as his own
the dancer in the cremation ground and in the golden hall
the thief who stole the heart
negations: beyond the reach of Brahmā and Viṣṇu, who could not find his crown and feet
relation_to_self: The devotee is his servant, son or friend; grace melts the heart; love of him is himself.
relation_to_world: He dwells in the named temples of the Tamil land; all the universes are motes before him.
caveat: Devotional, not scholastic; the hymns praise Śiva as supreme and reject Jain and Buddhist teaching.
